intro.title: Micro-frontend Shell
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a micro-frontend shell, which is a React application that acts as a container to host multiple smaller, independent frontend applications. You will learn the core concept of composing a user interface by dynamically loading and rendering different components based on navigation. The main technologies involved are React components, state management with the useState hook, and event handling. By the end, you will have a functional shell that can switch between micro-frontend views, demonstrating a foundational pattern for scalable web development.
intro.usecase: A micro-frontend shell acts as the main container application that dynamically loads and orchestrates multiple, independently developed frontend modules. This pattern is essential in large-scale products like enterprise dashboards, where different teams own separate panels for analytics, user management, or reporting, allowing for independent deployment and updates. It's also used in e-commerce platforms to seamlessly integrate distinct features such as product listings, shopping carts, and recommendation widgets into a single cohesive UI. For developers, this approach enables scalable, maintainable applications by decoupling feature development and reducing cross-team dependencies.
